title: High availability, read replicas and point-in-time recovery

videos.script: A database can fail in three ways. The machine can go, the region can go, or somebody can make a mistake. Each needs a different copy. {{three}} For the machine, there is high availability. A standby in another zone has every write on its disk before the commit returns. When the primary fails, the address moves to the standby. {{standby}} For reading, and for the region, there are read replicas. They answer queries, and they run a little behind. {{replica}} On your laptop you build one with PostgreSQL itself, the engine under Cloud SQL. You pause it, write a hundred orders, and watch it fall a hundred behind. {{lag}} Neither copy saves you from a DELETE without a WHERE. You will run one, and watch the replica copy it within the second. {{mistake}} For that, there is the log. You archive it, restore last night's backup, and replay it to the second before the mistake. {{recover}} Cloud SQL does the same as a clone, a new instance beside the old. And one restore surprises people. It overwrites the instance it goes to. {{restore}}
